question: Which year marked the completion of Rashtrapati Bhavan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1929**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The construction of the **Rashtrapati Bhavan**, originally known as the **Viceroy's House**, was completed in the year **1929**. The project was a massive undertaking that spanned nearly **17 years** from its inception to its final completion. **Hence, this option is correct.**

• The year **1912** marked the **commencement** of the construction work on **Raisina Hill**. This followed the **1911** announcement by **King George V** during the **Delhi Durbar** that the capital of **British India** would be shifted from **Calcutta** to **Delhi**. Hence, this option is incorrect as it refers to the start, not the completion.

• The year **1921** is significant in the history of **New Delhi** as the **foundation stone** of the **Council House** (now known as the **Old Parliament House** or **Sansad Bhavan**) was laid by the **Duke of Connaught**, but the **Viceroy's House** was still in the middle of its construction phase during this time. Hence, this option is incorrect.

• The year **1935** is historically important for the **Government of India Act 1935**, which introduced significant constitutional reforms. However, the **Rashtrapati Bhavan** had already been completed and occupied by the **Viceroy** for several years by then. Hence, this option is incorrect.

• The primary architect responsible for the design was **Sir Edwin Lutyens**, who worked alongside **Herbert Baker**. Lutyens was tasked with creating a residence that would symbolize the permanence of **British rule** in India, resulting in a structure that covers a floor area of **200,000 square feet**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Rashtrapati Bhavan** is the official residence of the **President of India** and is located at the Western end of **Rajpath** (now renamed **Kartavya Path**) in **New Delhi**. It is situated on **Raisina Hill**, which was leveled specifically for this project.

• The building comprises **four floors** and **340 rooms**, including the **Durbar Hall**, **Ashoka Hall**, and various guest suites. It is surrounded by a massive estate of **330 acres**, which includes the famous **Amrit Udyan** (formerly **Mughal Gardens**).

• The architectural style is a unique blend of **Mughal**, **Hindu**, and **Western Classical** influences. Notable Indian features include **chhatris** (dome-shaped pavilions), **jaalis** (perforated stone screens), and **chajjas** (overhanging eaves).

• The first resident of the building was **Lord Irwin**, the **Viceroy of India**, who moved into the house on **January 23, 1931**. After India gained independence, **C. Rajagopalachari** became the first Indian to reside there as the **Governor-General** in **1948**.

• On **January 26, 1950**, when India became a **Republic**, the building was officially renamed **Rashtrapati Bhavan**, and **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** became its first occupant in the capacity of the **President of India**.

**Important Points__**

• The central **dome** of the **Rashtrapati Bhavan** is one of its most striking features. It was inspired by the **Great Stupa at Sanchi**, showcasing the integration of **Buddhist architectural** elements into the design.

• The construction involved the use of approximately **700 million bricks** and **3 million cubic feet of stone**. The exterior is primarily made of **red and cream sandstone**, which was sourced from **Bharatpur** and **Dholpur**.

• The **Jaipur Column**, which stands in the center of the **Forecourt**, was a gift from the **Maharaja of Jaipur**, **Sawai Madho Singh**, to commemorate the building of the new capital city.

• The **Durbar Hall** is the most significant room within the building, located directly under the main dome. It is used for high-profile state ceremonies, such as the presentation of **Civilian and Military Awards** (like the **Bharat Ratna** and **Padma Awards**) and the **swearing-in** of the **Prime Minister** and the **Council of Ministers**.

• The **Ashoka Hall**, known for its magnificent **ceiling painting** and Persian-style carpets, serves as the venue for formal **State Banquets** and the credential ceremonies of **Foreign Ambassadors**.
